result:
Review complete. I ran 8 finder agents over the branch diff vs `main`, deduplicated ~40 candidate reports into 10 distinct claims, and adversarially verified each with a dedicated agent. The final report contains 10 findings (9 CONFIRMED, 1 PLAUSIBLE), ranked by severity.

The headline: the branch's fix — distinguishing an unavailable Lean verifier from a failed proof — only landed on the global pipeline. The decomposition/node path was missed in two independent ways: `formalizeNode` still collapses the result to `failed` (which then cascades through the auto-formalize queue, skipping all dependents), and the node status round-trip erases `unavailable` entirely, so none of the new UI ever appears in node mode. Separately, dropping the `localhost:3100` default breaks the documented docker-compose setup (nothing in the repo sets `LEAN_VERIFIER_URL`, and README/ARCHITECTURE/USER_GUIDE still describe the deleted default and mock fallback), and the live zustand store persists the transient `unavailable` status across reloads, contradicting the branch's own new sanitizer test.

Three candidates that looked plausible were refuted during verification and excluded: the "error wipe on re-verify" (pre-existing behavior; `main` was strictly worse with its false mock-pass), the divergent duplicate blocks in `useFormalizationPipeline` (they render identically — the fallback lives inside the retry loop), and the 35s abort-timer leak (pre-existing on `main`, negligible impact).
